questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres; Montenegro about 13,883 square kilometres; Kosovo about 10,909 square kilometres; Cyprus about 9,242 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which continent is North Macedonia in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find North Macedonia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find North Macedonia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture North Macedonia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: North Macedonia is bordered by Serbia, Albania, Greece and Bulgaria.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Skopje?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of North Macedonia is Skopje.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of North Macedonia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the North Macedonia article.

questions.proof: The capital and largest city is Skopje, with more than 500,000 residents.
